comparison: Compared rhbi-v5 against parent rhbi-v4 under protocol seed 0 on NVIDIA RTX A6000; single-factor ablation confirmed Weibull AKT + shock_mu=0.35 + fibre_rel_blend=0.7 preserve 4/4 regressed Tier-1 tasks identically to rhbi-v4 while settle_beta=22.0 at 0.22 caused all 4 regressions.
conclusion: Completed discriminator_stability Tier-1 seed-0 CUDA execution for rhbi-v5 (10 PASS, 5 FAIL). Weibull 1D AKT horizon normalization unlocked precision_gaussian_nvfp4 (PASS, cdf_ks=0.02344) and preserved precision_gaussian_mxfp8 (PASS, cdf_ks=0.03628), but rhbi_settle_beta=22.0 activated prematurely at residual < 0.22 (above thermal_tau=0.084), over-stiffening ebi_beta during active mode acquisition on ring16_acquisition, ae_gan_hold, model_ae_gan_multimodal, and model_vae_categorical.

decision_outcomes.reuse_note: Compatible original receipts; overlapping readouts are not independent runs or additive costs

hypothesis: Upgrading RHBI from rhbi-v4 to rhbi-v5 with Poisson-Weibull 1D AKT empirical OT horizon normalization (rhbi_akt_mode='weibull'), false-shock-proof thermal reopening (rhbi_thermal_shock_mu=0.35), state-driven settling Born-Infeld Lipschitz sharpness (rhbi_settle_beta=22.0), and row-local calibrated-relativistic conditional fibre critic blending (rhbi_fibre_rel_blend=0.7) preserves all 27/27 Tier 1 requirements and Tier 2 counted passes while tightening conditional residual_student alignment and passing quantized 1D NVFP4 acquisition under one global clock-free, shape-gate-free recipe on protocol seed 0.
next_action: Preserve rhbi-v5 readout as faithful negative/partial evidence and advance to rhbi-v6 gating settling Lipschitz sharpness strictly inside the thermal equilibrium regime.

study.competing_explanation: Expanding the 1D empirical OT horizon via Weibull quantile normalization or sharpening Born-Infeld Lipschitz walls during thermal settling could over-smooth 1D Gaussian modes under low-precision quantization or inflate 2D multimodal component covariance on ring16_acquisition if the settling ramp interacts with active mode capture.
